mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% annualized over the previous 3 months signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPIAUCSL annualized increase > 2% does not correlate with tighter monetary policy.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points over the previous 3 months signals a tightening labor market, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or UNRATE decrease > 0.5pp does not correlate with tightening labor market conditions.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% over the previous 3 months signals strengthening demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or HOUST increase > 5% does not correlate with economic expansion.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over the previous 3 months signals a contraction in supply, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as companies face increased costs and reduced output.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or INDPRO decrease > 1% does not correlate with economic contraction.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 0.5% signals an accommodative monetary policy, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%, or FEDFUNDS below 0.5% does not correlate with accommodative monetary policy.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 over the previous month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2 percentage points, it signals a strong labor market, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increase > 200k and UNRATE decrease > 0.2pp in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint condition does not correlate with a strong labor market.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) increase by more than 1% over the previous month and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) remains stable (less than 0.2% increase), it signals strong consumer demand without inflationary pressure, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increase > 1% and CPIAUCSL increase < 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint condition does not correlate with strong consumer demand without inflationary pressure.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) increases by more than 2% over the previous 3 months and GDP (GDPC1) also increases by more than 1% over the previous 6 months, it signals a robust expansion in supply and economic growth, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increase > 2% in 3 months and GDPC1 increase > 1% in 6 months
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint condition does not correlate with robust economic expansion.
